items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: And Ernest Rogers played the drum. He the one that brought me in.

ctx.x: I see. Well who decided about what part you should take?

Well, about the part I should have taken, it was undecided. They didn't know I could read. And Ernest Rogers played the drum. He the one that brought me in. They needed a man to play, so he recommended me, which he used to play in the brass band, in the Pacific band. And he recommended me to Wilson, so we got there, I could hear him talk, and they didn't know. This is one of them kids that's like, a kid playing, a kid somebody, or something like a kid. And so after they gave me the part and I played all right,…
Yeah. You know what I heard of him? Somewhere. Who else did he play with?

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1958-12-22
items.q: Ornis Rodgers. Yeah. Either one. Got me to come into the band.

ctx.x: And, or, or, or, or, or, or, Ornis Rodgers. Yeah. Either one. Got me to come into the band. And, uh, you know, Shots and Wilson, they were talking. A fella, you don't know him, but name called him, Guy Sooner. He's a big, big, big, big, big, big, time guy. You see. And so they was talking about what part to give me. I was just mad at him, Roger, say, give me the part. Don't worry. And that's how I got the band. So anyway, they put me on the first part. Yeah. And I played, and they were surprised. Be taking care…
Did you use quite a bit of music in those days? That's what I'm talking about.
